twist.question: Heavy rain falls on Mumbai. Will streets flood more at high tide or at low tide?
twist.reason: Mumbai's drains empty into the sea. At high tide the sea is up at the drain outlets, so rainwater can't get out.

faq.q: But WHY does the sea come and go?
faq.a: The Moon's gravity tugs on Earth's oceans, making a bulge of water. As Earth spins, your beach moves into the bulge and out again. Chief Detectives explore this later.
The sea can come in fast. Always check tide times with a grown-up before walking out.

faq.q: Are tides the same every day?
faq.a: No. They're about 50 minutes later each day, and some days they're bigger.

knowledgePack: Most coasts have two high tides and two low tides about every 24 hours 50 minutes, so each tide is about 50 minutes later than the day before. High tides are about 12 hours 25 minutes apart. Tides are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity, with help from the Sun; Earth's spin carries places into and out of the bulges of water. In Mumbai the difference between high and low tide can be several metres. Haji Ali's causeway is usable around low tide and covered around high tide. When heavy rain coincides with high tide, Mumbai floods more because water cannot drain to the sea.
